solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mechanical lift with placard banning outsiders

parts.note: to lift is slang for to steal, i.e. rob

indicators.note: banning the outsiders means the first and last letters of the placard word are dropped

parts.note: a placard is a posted notice

explanation.surface: A crane-like lift with a sign forbidding entry to people who don't belong there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banning outsiders' strips N and E from NOTICE, leaving OTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something robotic acts like a machine, without feeling or variation.

clue.text: Artistic impression — source of friction?

definitions.meaning: a ..., such as a brass ..., is an image made by ... over a surface

explanation.surface: A painted portrait that started an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'friction' suggests a quarrel but means physical resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass rubbings copy church memorials; rubbing surfaces is what produces friction.

clue.text: Skilled tribesmen might reveal this transport holding up companion on platform

parts.note: a bus is a means of transport

indicators.note: holding up, in a down entry, means the letters are lifted and read bottom to top

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour
a raft is a floating platform

explanation.surface: A bus carrying a friend up onto a stage is something skilled natives would show.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'holding up' turns the companion's letters upwards; CH is Companion of Honour, a British order.
explanation.definitionFit: Bushcraft is wilderness survival know-how, the kind of expertise forest-dwelling peoples possess.

clue.text: Workers organised prominent feature in school

parts.note: workers organised together form a trade union, TU
a tor is a rocky hill standing out on moorland

explanation.surface: Unionised staff set up the main attraction in a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is a verb here, to teach; a tor is a rocky outcrop on Dartmoor-type moorland.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to instruct them, which is what a tutor does as a verb.

clue.text: Criminal trial in confined space? It's near the bone

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the space word

parts.note: a cage is an enclosed space

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters of trial are crooked, out of order

explanation.surface: A court case held in a cramped room is close to the knuckle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' rearranges TRIAL to RTILA, put 'in' CAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cartilage is connective tissue found at the ends of bones and in joints.

clue.text: One in field at college concealing wrong

parts.note: cover is a cricket fielding position, so a fielder there is 'cover'
to be 'up' is to be in residence at a university such as Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A student playing in the field at college hides some misdeed.
explanation.walkthrough: COVER is a fielding position in cricket, on the off side of the batter.
explanation.definitionFit: A cover-up is the act of hiding a scandal or crime from public view.

clue.text: Schoolboy might have this fattened bird

definitions.meaning: a schoolboy might wear his school cap
a castrated cockerel fattened for eating

explanation.surface: A boy at school might be served a plump chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part only works split as CAP ON, a uniform cap being worn.
explanation.definitionFit: A capon is a castrated rooster raised for the table, so a fattened fowl.

clue.text: Model cover with no end of chic transformed cycling arena

indicators.note: transformed means the combined letters change their order completely
with no means that letter is removed from cover
end of picks the final letter of chic

explanation.surface: A model's outfit, lacking chic, is turned into a velodrome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no end of chic' drops C from COVER, leaving OVER; 'transformed' rearranges MODEL plus OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A velodrome is a banked track built for bicycle racing.

clue.text: Breed fish, we're told

indicators.note: we're told signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: rays are flat fish such as skates

explanation.surface: A tip on rearing fish, passed on by hearsay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we're told' signals the sound of RAYS.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise animals is to rear or breed them.

clue.text: Agent's work otherwise promoted unknown singer

parts.note: PR, public relations, is the work of a press agent

indicators.note: promoted in a down entry means the letters are raised, read upwards

parts.note: else means otherwise
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An agent's efforts pushed an obscure singer to fame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoted' reverses ELSE to ESLE in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Presley was the American singer known as the King of Rock and Roll.

clue.text: Get ready for attack

definitions.meaning: read as two words: be prepared

explanation.surface: An order to prepare before an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: Split as BE SET it means be prepared; as one word it means to harass or assail.

clue.text: Loathsome salesman lives freely behind university

indicators.note: behind says the following piece comes after the university letter

parts.note: a rep is a travelling sales representative

indicators.note: freely means the letters of lives are arranged without constraint

explanation.surface: A disgusting sales rep who lives without restraint near a campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' is the anagram signal, and 'behind' puts the rearranged letters after the university's U.
explanation.definitionFit: Repulsive and loathsome are synonyms: both describe something that provokes disgust.

clue.text: Cops in ruin stripped of power contrived hostile move

indicators.note: contrived means the remaining letters are artfully rearranged
stripped of means the power letter is taken away from the phrase

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Police ruined and powerless stage a hostile action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripped of' removes P from COPSINRUIN; 'contrived' rearranges what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: An incursion is a raid or invasion into enemy territory, an aggressive manoeuvre.

clue.text: Remain in Germany in fit condition

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)
being well means being healthy

explanation.surface: Advice to stay in Germany while one is healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to live or stay somewhere, so it can mean to remain.

clue.text: US composer in schooner, possibly

definitions.meaning: Philip ... is an American minimalist composer
a schooner is a tall drinking ... for sherry or beer

explanation.surface: An American composer aboard a sailing ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'schooner' suggests a sailing ship but here is a large drinking vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip Glass is a famous American minimalist; a schooner is one kind of drinking tumbler.

clue.text: Unofficial count? It might be taken in corridor entered by a heartless whip

indicators.note: entered by means the walk word has the other letters put inside it

parts.words: It might be taken in corridor
parts.note: a stroll is a walk, which one might take along a corridor

indicators.note: heartless means the middle of whip is cut out

explanation.surface: An informal tally, perhaps held in a hallway invaded by a cruel lash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes HI from WHIP, leaving WP; A plus WP is 'entered' into STROLL.
explanation.definitionFit: A straw poll is an informal vote taken to gauge opinion, not an official one.

clue.text: One's bound to show varied work?

definitions.text: One's bound to show varied work?

parts.words: One's bound to show varied work?
parts.note: read as a book bound to display a selection of different writings, not a person obliged to perform

explanation.surface: Someone is obliged to display a range of their output.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' seems to mean obliged, but it means bound in covers like a book.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthology is a bound collection of pieces by various writers.

clue.text: Figure cut quiet getting on level

indicators.note: cut means the figure loses its last letter

parts.note: three is a figure, a number
sh is a call for quiet
someone getting on is old

explanation.surface: A trimmed silhouette, quietly getting onto a flat surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks E from THREE.
explanation.definitionFit: A threshold is a level or point at which something starts to take effect.

clue.text: One immersed in contents of bin?

definitions.text: One immersed in contents of bin?

parts.words: One immersed in contents of bin?
parts.note: the bin is a wine bin, a rack of bottles, and one immersed in it loves wine, not rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone up to their neck in a rubbish bin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bin' suggests rubbish; a wine bin is a cellar storage rack.
explanation.definitionFit: An oenophile is a connoisseur and lover of wines.

clue.text: Winding route by river requiring jackets, say

indicators.note: a winding path twists, so the letters of route are twisted into a new order

parts.note: the Wear is a river in north-east England, through Durham

explanation.surface: A meandering path beside a river where coats are needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winding' rearranges ROUTE to OUTER; the Wear is a river in County Durham.
explanation.definitionFit: Jackets are an example of clothes worn over other garments, i.e. outer garments.

clue.text: Choose mail for redirecting? That's best

parts.note: to opt is to choose

indicators.note: letters sent for redirecting are sent along a different route, so mail is reordered

explanation.surface: Choosing to have post forwarded is the best plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for redirecting' rearranges MAIL to IMAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimal means most favourable, the best possible.

clue.text: German artist back cycling

indicators.note: cycling means letters go round from the front of the word to its end

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A German painter returns home by bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves ST from the front of STERN to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German-born Dada and Surrealist painter.

clue.text: Brown variant of dark drinking vessel

parts.note: tan is a brown colour

indicators.note: variant of means a different arrangement of the letters of dark

explanation.surface: Brown is a version of dark in a beer mug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variant of' rearranges DARK to KARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A tankard is a large beer mug, often of pewter, with a handle.

clue.text: Deliver wrongly spread on furniture

definitions.meaning: in cricket a bowler who ..., straightening the arm, delivers the ball illegally
a cloth draped over a sofa or bed

explanation.surface: A cover for a sofa that arrived by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, throwing is an illegal bowling action; a bowler must keep the arm straight.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing is an unlawful delivery in cricket; a throw is also a decorative blanket over a couch.

clue.text: Bishop penning a note that's less well done

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the bishop letters surround the rest

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A clergyman writing a short message that is not so well cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' looks like writing but means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Steak cooked rarer is cooked for less time, so less well done.

clue.text: Young woman with husband, a writer, is disfigured

parts.note: miss is a title for a young unmarried woman
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A girl, her spouse and an author: one of them is scarred.
explanation.definitionFit: Misshapen means deformed in shape, so a disfigured thing is misshapen.

clue.text: Originally, many ancients of Rotorua interacted — in this?

definitions.text: Originally, many ancients of Rotorua interacted — in this?

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Long ago, many old people of Rotorua conversed in their own language.
explanation.walkthrough: Rotorua is a town in New Zealand with a large Maori population.
explanation.definitionFit: Maori is the Polynesian language of New Zealand's indigenous people, spoken around Rotorua.

clue.text: Such a vocalist harbours mayhem

indicators.note: harbours means the phrase shelters the answer inside its letters

explanation.surface: That kind of singer is a source of chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harbours' holds the letters across 'Such a vocalist'.
explanation.definitionFit: Havoc and mayhem are synonyms for widespread chaos and destruction.

clue.text: Married policeman blocks faceless wine merchant

indicators.note: blocks means the officer sits in the middle, obstructing the wine word
faceless means the wine name loses its first letter, its face

parts.note: Barolo is a red wine from Piedmont
a cop is a policeman

explanation.surface: A married officer obstructs an anonymous wine dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faceless' drops the wine's first letter; 'blocks' puts the policeman inside what remains. 'wine merchant' looks like the definition, but only 'merchant' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Marco Polo was a Venetian trader whose travels reached the court of Kublai Khan.

clue.text: There you are retired in Bali overindulging

indicators.note: retired says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer lies within the letters of the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone has withdrawn into excess while on holiday in Bali.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' as a link word, but 'in' is what marks the hidden letters, so it is now the indicator. 'retired' then reads the hidden letters backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Voilà is the French exclamation used in English when presenting something finished.

clue.text: Role played by Italian author, not very alluring figure

indicators.note: played suggests the letters of role are acted out in a new order
not says the very letter is taken out of the author's name

parts.note: Primo Levi was an Italian writer

explanation.surface: A part acted by an Italian writer who was not very attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' turns ROLE into LORE; 'not very' drops V from LEVI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lorelei is a siren of German legend who lured Rhine boatmen to their doom.

clue.text: Trim dress old actor ordered

indicators.note: trim says the end is cut off the dress word

parts.note: to deck is to dress up, as in deck out
Oliver Reed was an English actor who died in 1999

explanation.surface: An instruction to tidy the outfit of a veteran performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trim' looks like the verb to tidy but cuts K from DECK.
explanation.definitionFit: To decree is to order officially, so decreed is ordered.
